To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the HSQC‐TOC‐SY and HSQC‐ NOESY experiments are useful tools in the analysis of 1H‐1H COSY and NOE spectra, and that the combination of NMR, DFT‐GIOA chemical shielding calculations, and molecular modeling is a powerful method for structure determination of slowly exchanging molecules in solution.
the combination of NMR and computational modeling provides a unique opportunity to study conformational equilibria in solution, and to determine the structure of individual conformers.
the use of HSQC‐NOE experiments, in combination with DFT‐GIOA chemical shielding calculations, provides a powerful approach for the structural determination of slowly exchanging molecules.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development and application of NMR spectroscopy to the study of organic and organometallic compounds, particularly in the areas of structure determination, stereochemistry and conformational analysis, reaction monitoring and mechanism, as well as the study of dynamic processes.
the development and application of high‐resolution N‐methyl NMR techniques to the structural elucidation of complex organic molecules.
the application of NMR and theoretical chemical shift calculations to the determination of the structure of slowly exchanging conformational isomers of a complex molecule in solution.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
HSQC‐TOC‐SY and HSQC‐TOESY experiments can offer solutions for overlap and assignment problems in COSY‐ and NOESY‐type spectra, respectively.

the combination of high‐resolution Nuclei‐Nuclei correlation spectroscopy (COSY) and nuclear Overhauser enhancement spectroscopy (NOESY) experiments, with the use of the recently introduced HSQC‐TOC SY and HSQC‐N OESY pulse sequences, can be a valuable alternative to 2D N‐C correlation spectroscopy (HMQC, HSQC) and NOESY‐HMQC/HSQC experiments.

the use of the HSQC‐TOC‐SY and NOESY experiments is highly recommended for the assignment of complex 1H‐1H‐13C‐13C spectra of small molecules, and in particular for the assignment of the 1H and/or 13C resonances that give rise to severe overlap problems in the 1H‐ and 13C‐NMR spectra.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
NMR is a powerful tool for structural determination of molecules, and it is a very useful tool for structural determination.
we have shown that the combination of NMR, molecular modeling, and DFT calculations is an effective way to determine the structure of molecules in solution.
we have shown that the interplay of NMR spectroscopy and computational modeling can lead to the determination of the structure of slowly exchanging conformations.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of DFT‐G‐IAO calculations of chemical shielding in conjunction with high‐field NMR spectroscopy can lead to a significant improvement in structure determination of slowly exchanging systems.
the combination of high‐resolution N‐MR and DFT‐calculated shielding is an effective strategy to determine the structure of slowly exchanging conformer mixtures in solution.
the interplay of NMR and quantum mechanical calculations can provide detailed structural information for complex molecules.
